episodes.165256: Isolated strong thunderstorms produced sub severe hail up to the size of pennies in the Table Rock Lake region of southern Missouri.
episodes.165281: In addition to severe weather, excessive rainfall occurred causing numerous locations to experience flash flooding.  ||4-5.5 inches of rain in southern middle Tennessee.|20 roads closed due to flash flooding in Moore County alone.|Several roads closed in Lincoln County.|Schools closed on the 23rd as a result.
episodes.166161: An area of low pressure moved across the region bringing mild and windy weather along with periods of rainfall, some heavy enough, to cause localized areas of flooding. An ice jam also developed in the Village of Dolgeville leading to flooding along the East Canada Creek.
episodes.166803: A deep low pressure system drew warm and moist air into western Virginia from the Gulf of Mexico, and produced rounds of light to occasionally moderate rainfall across Smyth County over a 3-day period, with the most substantial rainfall occurring on February 24th.    Rainfall rates were observed approaching 1 inch per hour at times. The rainfall affected mainly the smaller creeks and streams, though multiple stream gauges for the larger rivers of the Holston basin remained within Action Stage and did not leave their banks.  The lack of flooding had much to do with local streamflows measuring below-normal to well below-normal, given the lack of precipitation for several weeks prior to this event.
episodes.166886: A moist southwesterly flow aloft ran nearly parallel to a stalled cold front near east Tennessee on the 23rd. A surface low near Lake Charles LA would move up the boundary and produce a second round of rains on the 24th.
episodes.166901: Scattered storms developed during the afternoon and brought hail and damaging winds to portions of central Mississippi.

events.narrative: Rainfall of up to four inches fell which resulted in street flooding throughout Starkville and surrounding areas of the county.
Road closed due to flooding on Main Street. Depth of water unknown.
Goose Branch Road was closed due to flooding. Depth of water unknown.
Coker Road closed due to flooding. Depth of water unknown.
Powell Hollow Road was closed due to flooding. Depth of water unknown.

An ice jam blocking the Sacandaga River broke, causing an increase in water downstream and flooded multiple homes along River Road in the Town of Hope. Four individuals and one dog were rescued by New York State Forest Rangers.
Minor flooding was reported near Gray.
Penny sized hail was reported.
Flooding reported on Tazewell Pike.
Flooding reported across the southern portion of the county, including Bulls Gap.
Numerous roads were flooded and several were impassable across the county.
Hail up to pennies in size was reported.
Minor flooding was occurring on several roadways across the county, but no known road closures yet.
Flooding near the intersection of White Avenue and Colonial Drive. The road was being monitored for possible closure.
About a one hundred foot long stretch of Tarpine Valley Road was covered by flowing water near its intersection with state Road 70.
Raccoon Valley Drive was flooded.

The Smyth County 911 Center reported minor flooding of small creeks and streams at various locations across the county during the afternoon and evening of the 24th due to prolonged rainfall atop saturated soils.  A few roads had several inches of standing water on them, causing lanes of traffic to be closed for brief periods of time.  No damage was reported.
Several roads were closed due to flooding, mainly across the western half of the county including Kingsport, but also in Bluff City.
State Road 160 was flooded between Bybee Road and Pine Ridge Way.
Kidwell Ridge Road was flooded along the creek crossing.
Forty roads remained flooded across the county, with numerous closures now reported. Two feet of water covered Old Baileytown Road near North Greene High School.
High water observed on roadway near Laurel Bloomery, but road was still passable.
